limitations: Native requirement mapping is preserved; independent semantic coverage and targeted positive/negative/equivalent game fixtures have not been qualified.

requirements.obligation: Fresh launch or Restart
Enter play
Begin with 170 coins, an intact 500-health crystal, four unoccupied gold deposits, zero defenses and zero completed waves.
No enemy or projectile exists.
Speed is 1x.
No carried-over income, purchases, damage or selection.
The coin counter and instruction to build a mine are visible.
Reopen has the same fresh progress state.
Boundaries: 6.2.4.
Round visible
View the field
Present a fixed elevated three-quarter 3D view of a square brown clearing surrounded by bright green grass, conifers, bushes, flowers, scattered stones and a left-side dirt approach.
Keep the entire build area and crystal visible at 1280 x 720 and 1920 x 1080.
No flat diagram, unlit graybox, empty background, clipped board or camera needed to find a legal build cell.
Use bright directional daylight, soft cast shadows and saturated green/brown terrain.
The camera reveals both the tops and sides of structures, with the pink-red crystal prominent near the center of the clearing.
The build sidebar remains separate from actionable world space.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
New round
Inspect or place on the clearing
Use a 20 x 20 square logical build grid with zero-based (column, row) coordinates from 0 through 19, rows increasing toward the bottom of the screen and columns to the right.
The crystal occupies (10,10).
One cell is 200 world-distance units for the balance values below.
No placements outside this clearing, on the crystal or on scenery.
The grid may be subtle or only shown during placement; the hovered cell is unambiguous.
Coordinates specify player-facing board layout, not an engine-axis convention.
Boundaries: 6.2.5.
Preparation, countdown, combat or rest
Left-click a build icon
Select exactly one of Mine, Archer Tower, Cannon Tower or Wall.
Show its name, current price and selection highlight.
Selecting a different type replaces the prior selection.
Selection alone spends no coins and creates no building.
Distinct icons in a vertically arranged left build panel.
Controls work during combat without pausing the world.
Boundaries: 6.2.4.
A build type is selected
Move the pointer over the board
Show a snapped translucent model preview at the hovered cell, with green for legal and red for illegal placement.
Towers also show their attack-radius preview.
Preview objects cannot block, attack, produce income, take damage or count as buildings.
Preview follows the pointer and displays the actual footprint.
Leaving the board or hovering UI hides the world preview; colors have an additional outline or readable validity cue.
Boundaries: 6.2.4.
Placement preview or building details open
Right-click or press Escape
Cancel the current selection and close its preview/details.
No purchase, sale, damage, refund or pause is caused by cancel.
Selection highlight, range ring and preview disappear.
Repeated cancel is harmless
Escape on a clean play view is a no-op.
Boundaries: 6.2.4.
A selected defense has an empty legal cell and sufficient coins
Left-click that cell
Create one level-1 building, deduct its displayed current price exactly once, and begin a short rise/pop construction animation lasting 0.15-0.6 simulation seconds.
No duplicate building or second charge from a held button.
The solid model replaces the preview, coins update and a build cue plays.
The selected build type remains available for repeated placements.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.7.
Any placement restriction fails
Left-click an occupied, reserved, out-of-bounds or unaffordable cell
Reject the purchase while keeping coins, ownership and prices unchanged.
No overlap stacking, partial purchase or negative balance.
Show a visible placement or affordability reason within 0.2 real seconds.
Exactly enough coins permits a valid purchase; holding or repeatedly clicking an illegal cell cannot charge.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.7.
Mine selected
Left-click a gold deposit
Only an unoccupied deposit permits a mine.
Replace its exposed rock silhouette with the built mine while preserving its board location.
No mine on ordinary soil, second mine on one deposit or unrelated defense on an exposed deposit.
The construction changes the deposit silhouette.
Selling or destroying the mine exposes its deposit again.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.7.
Any active round
Build, sell or lose a building
Current price equals base price plus increment times the number of currently living player-owned buildings of that type: Mine 0 + 600 each
Archer 20 + 15 each
Cannon 25 + 20 each
Wall 5 + 2 each.
No cross-type price changes or price below its base.
Build-panel prices update immediately after the ownership change.
Upgrading does not add a building to the count.
Boundaries: 6.2.7.
An intact mine exists
Every 10 simulation seconds of that mine's life
Credit 25 + 8 times completed-wave count coins to the shared wallet.
Each mine has its own cycle; the first payout is after a full interval.
No idle income before a mine exists, double payout or payout after the mine is removed.
Gold-colored floating +amount text rises above the mine and the wallet updates.
The current completed-wave count at payout determines the amount; pausing freezes the cycle.
A built structure is visible
Left-click it while no build type is selected
Open contextual details with type, level, current/max health, refund amount and, for towers, damage, cooldown, range and the next upgrade price or maximum-level state.
The inspection click must not build, sell or upgrade.
Place the readable detail card near the selected structure without hiding critical controls; show a tower range ring.
Selecting another building replaces the card; clicking empty ground clears it.
Boundaries: 6.2.7.
A fully constructed level-1 or level-2 tower is selected and coins cover its upgrade
Left-click Upgrade
Pay 200 to reach level 2 or 600 to reach level 3; apply the corresponding balance row immediately.
No skipped level, free upgrade or duplicate charge from one click.
Change both tower body and weapon to their distinct tier meshes, play an upgrade effect and update details.
Levels are displayed as 1, 2 and 3.
Boundaries: 6.2.7, 6.2.8.
A tower is damaged
Complete a legal upgrade
Preserve health percentage: new health = old health / old maximum times new maximum.
No unconditional full heal and no health above the new maximum.
Health bar and detail values reflect the new amount.
Fractional health is valid; displayed numbers may round without altering the underlying value.
Boundaries: 6.2.7.
Insufficient coins, maximum tower tier, construction in progress, or a mine/wall
Attempt Upgrade
Leave balance, tier, models, health and timers unchanged.
Mines and walls have no upgrades.
No invisible or unaffordable upgrade and no tier above 3.
Unavailable controls are disabled or explain the reason.
Repeated rejection remains safe.
Boundaries: 6.2.7.
A player-owned structure is selected
Left-click Sell
Remove it once and refund floor(50% of the amount paid to place that object).
Upgrades are not refunded.
Recompute current build prices.
No refund for the crystal, an exposed deposit, enemies, already removed structures or their upgrades.
Show the refund before sale; close details and remove its health bar and range ring after sale.
The first free mine refunds zero.
A refunded mine leaves a reusable deposit.
Boundaries: 6.2.7, 6.2.8.
A living owned building or crystal has missing health
Simulation advances
Regenerate 2 health per simulation second, clamped to that object's maximum.
Walls have 450 health, mines 1500, and the crystal 500.
Tower maxima are in the table below.
No regeneration after destruction or during pause/defeat; no overheal.
World-space health bars truthfully track damage and regeneration.
Health can be fractional.
Regeneration does not restore a removed object.
A non-crystal structure reaches zero health
Enemy damage resolves
Remove its gameplay presence, ownership count, collision and active actions; restore the deposit if it was a mine.
Give no sale refund.
No lingering invisible blocker, stale attacker target, income payout or newly released tower shot after removal.
Already airborne projectiles follow COMBAT-01.
Play a destruction effect and clear any details for that object.
Its former attackers can continue toward the crystal or another obstruction.
Boundaries: 6.2.7, 6.2.8.
No mine has yet been built in a new round
Wait or place non-mine defenses
Remain in preparation indefinitely with no enemies and no wave countdown progress.
Building the first mine starts a 2-second countdown to wave 1.
No wave starts merely from time, selecting Mine or an invalid mine placement.
Replace the mine instruction with a visible upcoming-wave countdown.
After the first valid mine starts the round, later mine loss does not return to the initial waiting gate.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.6.
The round is counting down
Countdown expires
Start the next wave, play one horn cue and emit exactly its scheduled enemies at evenly spaced times across its spawn duration.
Enemies enter from its enabled grass edges and move into view.
No overspawn, skipped groups or pre-countdown spawn.
Show current wave and remaining enemies.
For N enemies over T simulation seconds, emission k occurs at k times T/N, for k from 1 to N.
The first occurs at T/N and the last at T.
The single enemy of wave 24 enters at 0.1 seconds; rest has no emissions.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.6.
A scheduled wave starts
Run that wave
Use all 25 wave compositions, enemy tiers, spawn durations and enabled sides in Section 6.2.3.
North, South, West and East refer to the corresponding screen edges.
No shortened substitute campaign, omitted flying species, replaced boss wave or reduced enemy counts.
Enemy species and tiers visibly differ.
Wave 11 is an 8-second rest with no enemies, then counts as cleared.
Tier labels in the tables are 1-based.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.6.
A combat wave is in progress
The final scheduled enemy dies
Clear the wave only after every scheduled enemy has spawned and no living enemy remains.
Increment completed waves once and begin a fresh 2-second inter-wave countdown.
No clear while enemies remain unspawned, no duplicate completed-wave increment or next-wave overlap.
The HUD changes from combat to the next countdown.
The rest wave uses its own duration.
A defeat on the same update takes priority over wave clearance.
Wave 25 has been cleared
Continue survival
Continue indefinitely using wave 25's composition.
For wave w > 25, each group has floor(base_count times (1 + 0.2 times (w - 25)) + 0.5) members, all at tier 3.
Preserve its spawn duration and four-side attacks.
No victory screen or automatic reset after the fixed schedule.
Wave count and survival progress keep increasing.
Calculate remaining count from the actual integer group counts; no fractional or negative remaining enemies.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.6.
Fresh launch with the same configured seed
Repeat the same timed player inputs
Generate the same wave group ordering and spawn locations.
Default seed is 50; another nonnegative 32-bit seed may alter ordering/locations but not counts, stats, prices or the board.
No deterministic seed that changes the rules or disables ordinary play.
All spawned enemies remain legible and enter via enabled edges.
No exact random-number algorithm or exact coordinate sequence is required across different implementations.
Boundaries: 6.2.6.
Slime, Skeleton or Orc spawned
Simulation advances
Ground enemies travel toward the crystal; if a living structure obstructs their advance, stop and attack it until it is removed, then resume.
Use the species/tier stats in Section 6.2.2.
No movement through living walls/defenses, attacking removed targets or off-map stationary mobs that prevent clearance.
Ground walk/run, attack and death animations communicate their state.
Contact with the crystal causes attacks rather than instant deletion or single-use damage.
Boundaries: 6.2.5.
Bat or Dragon spawned
Simulation advances
Fly visibly above the ground toward the crystal, ignoring mines, walls and towers as movement blockers.
Attack the crystal when in contact.
Use Section 6.2.2 stats.
No landing merely to bypass targeting rules; a cannon cannot damage either flying species.
Flying silhouettes, wing motion and height distinguish them from ground enemies.
Their movement and attacks stop during pause/defeat; dead flyers cannot attack.
Boundaries: 6.2.5.
A living enemy is in contact with its target
Reach an attack interval
Apply its damage immediately on first contact, then no more than once per 1.0 simulation second while contact remains.
Switching targets or briefly leaving contact cannot bypass this per-enemy interval.
No frame-rate-scaled repeated hits, damage before contact, or attack by a dead enemy.
Animate the attack and update the affected health bar.
Switching targets does not multiply the attack rate; targets reaching zero resolve their removal.
An enemy reaches zero health
Resolve death
Award its tier's bounty once unless defeat has priority at that same simulation time.
Decrement the living/remaining count once, stop its attack and targetability immediately, then remove the corpse after its visible death animation.
No repeated bounty from splash, multiple projectiles or animation completion.
Show death motion and gold-colored +bounty text.
A corpse may finish visually but cannot delay a wave that has no living enemies.
Boundaries: 6.2.8.
An intact archer tower has an eligible enemy within 1000 ground-plane distance units (5 cells)
Its weapon is ready
Automatically aim at the nearest living ground or flying enemy and release a visible arrow.
Use the tier damage and cooldown table.
No shot at dead, nonexistent or out-of-range targets; no firing before construction completes.
The ballista turns toward its target and shows a firing/recoil motion.
A tied nearest enemy may be selected by any stable rule; idle readiness must not accumulate a burst.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.6.
An arrow has been released
The projectile travels and collides
Use visibly finite travel at 3000 distance units per simulation second.
Apply the tier's damage once on contact with one eligible living enemy and consume the projectile.
No damage at release, through unrelated geometry, or more than one single-target hit.
The arrow path and impact can be seen; the health change follows impact.
Leading a moving target is allowed; a miss expires safely within 4 simulation seconds.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.7.
A fully constructed intact cannon tower has a living ground enemy within 1000 ground-plane units
Its weapon is ready
Aim at the nearest eligible ground target and release a visible cannonball using the tier damage/cooldown table.
No targeting a Bat or Dragon, off-range enemy or corpse.
The cannon barrel aims and recoils; its projectile is visually distinct from an arrow.
No burst from accumulated idle cooldown.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.6.
A cannonball is in flight
It first hits ground, a blocking structure or an eligible ground target
Explode once at the impact point.
Damage each living ground enemy within the tier radius once; leave enemies outside the radius and all flying enemies unchanged.
Use finite travel at 3000 units per simulation second.
No repeated explosion from one impact, pre-impact damage or doubled direct-hit damage.
Show a colored burst, expanding shock ring/smoke and an explosion cue.
The radius is measured in the ground plane; an enemy exactly on its boundary is included.
Misses expire within 4 seconds.
Boundaries: 6.2.5, 6.2.7.
Any concurrent damage, sale, construction or wave event
Resolve the event
Keep ownership, wallet, health, enemy counts and targets consistent.
Projectiles already released continue after their tower is sold or destroyed, retaining release-time damage and splash radius.
No double death award, damage to a reused identity, negative enemy counts or lost enemies from an invalid target.
Visible objects and HUD remain consistent.
Upgrades preserve any remaining current cooldown.
The next shot uses the new tier and starts that tier's cooldown.
Times mean simulation time unless labeled real.
Isolated event timing tolerance is 0.15 seconds without cumulative rate drift; movement/range tolerance is 2% of specified distance.
Currency, counts, damage and tiers are exact.
The tolerance does not permit damage before visible impact or skipping phase boundaries.
Real-time UI limits keep their stated bounds.
Preparation, countdown, combat or rest
Hold F, then release it
While F is held, advance game simulation at 3x; return to 1x on release.
Movement, wave timers, weapons, regeneration, income and effects share the multiplier.
No permanent speed change from key repeat, separate accelerated income, or acceleration of UI input.
Display the active speed clearly.
Pause, defeat, focus loss and Restart release the fast-forward state.
Boundaries: 6.2.4.
A living active round
Press P or use the Pause/Resume control
Toggle a pause that freezes simulation and preserves all current progress.
Resume continues the same state.
No income, movement, spawning, cooldown, damage or regeneration while paused; no build, upgrade or sale.
A readable pause overlay and Resume/Restart controls remain operable.
Restart and exiting remain possible while paused; holding P does not repeatedly toggle.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.8.
The crystal reaches zero health
Resolve lethal damage
Enter defeat once, clamp crystal health to zero and stop gameplay simulation.
Display Game Over, completed waves and the wave reached.
No false victory, negative crystal health or later wave start.
Show a prominent result panel over the field and crystal destruction feedback.
Defeat has priority over simultaneous final-enemy death.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.8.
Game Over visible
Wait or attempt gameplay inputs
Keep wallet, wave progress, surviving gameplay entities and timers fixed after terminal damage/death resolution; disable building, upgrade, sale, attack and speed controls.
No in-flight projectile, delayed gameplay event or mine payout changes the result.
Restart and Exit remain visible and usable.
Repeated clicks do not create extra panels or reset progress.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.8.
Preparation, countdown, combat, rest, pause or defeat
Press R or click Restart
Start a fresh round matching START-01 without restarting the process.
No old buildings, enemies, corpses, projectiles, feedback text, selection, timer or queued input affecting the new round.
The fresh board and mine instruction reappear within 1 real second.
Repeated Restart, including during a projectile flight or payout boundary, still creates exactly one clean round.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.8.
Any round has changed progress
Close the process and launch again
Start from START-01 with no persisted run progress.
No recovered coins, purchased towers, lost crystal health, wave number or fast-forward state.
The opening screen matches a first launch.
Saving preferences is optional; it must not change required game progress.
Boundaries: 6.2.8.
Any playable state
View the HUD
Show coins at top left, build choices on the left, current wave/countdown and survival progress near the top, and accessible Pause/Restart/Exit controls.
All visible counters reflect actual state within 0.2 real seconds.
Use the supplied Baloo font for HUD text, Icon-Coin for currency, and GoldMine, ArcherTower, CannonTower and Wall textures for their build choices.
No obscured text, placeholder counters, replacement font/build icons or click-through from UI into world placement.
Use large rounded light text with a dark outline/shadow, dark translucent panels, gold coin imagery and distinct selected/disabled states.
Health and detail cards remain readable at both supported resolutions; font size, icon framing, tint and panel layout may be adjusted.
Boundaries: 6.2.4, 6.2.9.
A building or enemy has changed health
View the field or selected object
Render proportional world-space health bars for damaged enemies/structures and the crystal; keep values consistent with their current and maximum health.
No health bars attached to removed/reused objects or health bars presenting one object's health as another's.
A filled/empty contrast makes loss and regeneration visible.
Full-health bars may be hidden until hover/selection, except the living crystal's health bar stays visible.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
A legal or illegal player action occurs
Observe its immediate response
Use a distinct positive cue for build/upgrade/sale and a readable reason for invalid placement, insufficient money or unavailable upgrade.
No invisible rejection, stuck tooltip or feedback obscuring subsequent inputs.
Temporary text/effects clear; hover never spends coins.
Action feedback arrives within 0.2 real seconds; a UI click never also acts on the board beneath it.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
The field is assembled
Observe the scene
Use the supplied crystal/pedestal, mine/deposit, archer bodies/ballistae, cannon bodies/barrels and wall models as the primary visible structures.
Preserve all three tower tiers and their distinct silhouettes, materials and proportions.
No replacing these required models with cubes, sprites, text or identical tier skins.
The floating/spinning pink-red gem remains the focal point; structures sit on the ground and cast coherent shadows.
Material tuning, instancing, reorganization and equivalent visual effects are allowed; these are presentation assets, not prebuilt gameplay.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
Enemies are present
Run their movement, attack and death states
Use the supplied Slime, Skeleton, Orc, Bat and Dragon meshes, skeletons and suitable animation clips.
Preserve green slime, bone skeleton, bulky orc and winged bat/dragon identity; tiers use the supplied material/scale variation from Section 6.2.2.
No static sliding enemies, T-poses, mismatched skeletons or missing materials.
Locomotion, attack and death remain visually legible in a crowded wave.
Equivalent blends and animation timing are allowed if they preserve the specified rules.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
A round is rendered
View opening, placement and combat
Assemble the supplied ground/grass textures, trees, bushes, flowers, stones and fence assets into the scene described by SCENE-01.
Retain a generous green border around the central dirt field and layered vegetation.
No raw-asset gallery, featureless plane, giant background props blocking play or missing environment.
Place tall conifers along the outer edges, with lower shrubs, flower patches and stones between them and the clearing.
Keep the central build cells unobstructed and the left dirt approach readable; vegetation must provide foreground and background depth.
Exact decorative instance counts/coordinates are free.
Assemble the environment from pieces; no finished map is supplied.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
Construction, firing, impact, income or upgrade occurs
Observe its presentation
Provide construction rise/pop, weapon aim/recoil, arrows/cannonballs, impact flashes, cannon shock/smoke, upgrade glow, floating gold text and a pulsing placement/range cue.
No full-screen flash replacing spatial effects, permanent particles or decorative effects used as false hit confirmation.
Effects occur at the correct world object and remain readable above the field.
Create these effects using the provided textures/materials or equivalent legal effects; game logic remains independent of their implementation.
Boundaries: 6.2.8, 6.2.9.
Normal play with audio enabled
Perform a gameplay action and use the audio toggle
Provide background music and audible event feedback.
Supplied music and event-cue files are available.
Muting must not disable gameplay or its visual feedback.
The player can mute and restore audio while continuing to play.
Equivalent legally clear audio is permitted; exact cue waveforms, individual event coverage and onset latency are not acceptance criteria.
Boundaries: 6.2.9.
The project can start, run, exit and start again using the public instructions.
The main flow uses normal player input, without answer buttons, cheat entries or direct result shortcuts.
Key entry points, text and controls are visible, discoverable, readable and operable.
Player actions have perceptible feedback that agrees with the real game state.
No severe error blocks the main flow.
Repeated runs under the same initial conditions are substantially stable.

qualification_test_scope: Distribution, evidence conversion and attribution invariants only; not gameplay semantic qualification.
